spec.prompt: createWarning crashes with an unhelpful TypeError ('code.toUpperCase is not a function') when code is not a string, and silently accepts a non-string name or message. Validate them. For each of name, code and message: a missing value (undefined), null or '' keeps throwing the existing Error 'Warning <field> must not be empty'; any other value that is not a string (numbers including 0, booleans including false, objects, arrays) throws an Error with message 'Warning <field> must be a string'. Valid strings behave as before.
spec.requirement: createWarning checks name, code and message in that order. A field that is undefined, null or '' throws new Error('Warning <field> must not be empty'); a field that is any other non-string value (including 0, false, NaN, objects and arrays) throws new Error('Warning <field> must be a string'). Both are plain Errors. Valid input behaves as before (code is upper-cased).
spec.adjudication_rules: Score pass only if every hidden check passes. No partial credit; behaviour outside the requirement is not graded.

Prompt, requirement, oracle criteria, repository and base_rev, hidden suite, reference and incorrect implementations are unchanged. v1 stays frozen in bench/specs.lock.json; v1 and v2 results are never combined.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: code: 123 throws an Error with message 'Warning code must be a string'
name: {} throws 'Warning name must be a string'; message: 42 throws 'Warning message must be a string'; an array code is rejected the same way
falsy non-strings are not 'empty': code: 0 and message: false throw 'must be a string'
undefined, null and '' still throw 'Warning <field> must not be empty'
valid string fields create a working warning
